item.title: A BMO Extension of Oskolkov's Criterion for Rectangular Trigonometric Fourier Sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.17436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a sufficient condition in terms of sectional BMO for almost everywhere Pringsheim convergence of rectangular trigonometric Fourier sums. For continuous functions, the condition includes Oskolkov's criterion, and an example shows that the inclusion is strict.
item.dc:creator: Ushangi Goginava

item.title: On discrete harmonic functions with non-negativity on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An improvement of Liouville's theorem for discrete harmonic functions on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ was obtained by Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin. Namely, they proved that if a discrete harmonic function is bounded on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then the function is constant. In this paper, we study the corresponding problem if we replace the boundedness assumption with non-negativity. We establish this non-negativity result in some classes of discrete harmonic functions (polynomial growth and finite-translation-rank). Moreover, we prove that if a discrete harmonic function is non-negative on a large portion of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, then it has at most exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Gaitan Montejo, Carlos Garz\'on, Jos\'e Madrid

item.title: Sampling recovery for intersections of Lipschitz classes in the low-smoothness regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.17531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sampling recovery in $L_p(\mathbb T^d)$ for intersections of Lipschitz classes defined by smoothness conditions in two different metrics $L_p$ and $L_q$, where $1\le p<q\le\infty$. Our focus is on the low-smoothness range, where the $L_p$-smoothness does not exceed the classical continuity threshold $d/p$. We determine the exact orders of the sampling numbers for both linear and general recovery algorithms, including critical smoothness cases in which logarithmic factors appear or uniform convergence fails. To analyze sampling approximation in the low-smoothness range, we establish new inequalities for averaged moduli of smoothness with different integrability parameters and derive sharp estimates for these moduli and the corresponding semi-discrete measures of smoothness. These estimates provide error bounds for linear sampling operators acting on functions whose smoothness may lie below the classical continuity threshold. Finally, we determine the Kolmogorov widths of the intersection classes and quantify the gap between optimal sampling recovery and approximation by finite-dimensional subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Yurii Kolomoitsev

item.title: End-line Fourier restriction for hyperbolic surfaces in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove new bilinear adjoint Fourier restriction estimates for pairs of separated rectangles associated to a hyperbolic surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then employ these bilinear estimates to prove Fourier extension inequalities along the (sharp) parabolic scaling line for any smooth hyperbolic 2-surface that is either the graph of a polynomial or that obeys a mild finite type condition.
item.dc:creator: Sam Craig, Betsy Stovall

item.title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
item.description: arXiv:2611.18061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale H\"older family.
item.dc:creator: Xi Cen

item.title: On the spectrality of non-homogeneous self-similar measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.18106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-cylinder difference-set obstruction to the existence of an exponential orthonormal basis for a compactly supported probability measure. This obstruction uses the equal-scale and equal-mass structure of finitely many disjoint affine copies of the measure, together with Parseval's identity and an elementary atom bound for positive measures. We apply it to prove that the golden-mean self-similar measure generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/4$ is non-spectral. Together with a weight-rigidity argument, this excludes spectrality for every positive choice of weights in this iterated function system. We also analyze a logarithmically incommensurable example generated by $x/2$ and $(x+2)/3$, proving non-spectrality for all first-branch weights $p\in[1/3,5/6]$, including the natural weights. The latter proof reduces to two finite, exactly checkable integer difference-set conditions; an independent verification program is included in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Qiu Mao, Zhi-Yi Wu

item.title: What is... An Exceptional Set Estimate?
item.description: arXiv:2611.18250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exceptional set estimates are a fundamental topic of interest in projection theory. We introduce the topic through discrete geometry, and use this perspective to motivate some key results in the realm of geometric measure theory. To appear in the "What is?" series in the Notices of the AMS.
item.dc:creator: Paige Bright, Krystal Taylor

item.title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Antezana, Luciano Scazzola

item.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
item.description: arXiv:2611.16156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Fischler, Li Lai, Johannes Sprang, Wadim Zudilin

item.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.17640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.
item.dc:creator: Carrie Clark, Richard S. Laugesen

item.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
item.description: arXiv:2611.17750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Rational Solutions of Abel Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2109.07853v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the rational solutions of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$ where $A$ and $B \in \mathbb{C}[t]$. We prove that if $\deg(A)$ is even or $\deg(B)>(\deg(A)-1)/2$ then the equation has at most two rational solutions. For any other case, an upper bound on the number of rational solutions is obtained. Moreover, we prove that if there are more than $(\deg(A)+1)/2$ rational solutions then the equation admits a Darboux first integral.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 515 (2022), 126368
item.dc:creator: J. L. Bravo, L. A. Calder\'on, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda

item.title: Dimension-free Fourier restriction inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2412.03942v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ denote the best constant for the $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\to L^q(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ Fourier restriction inequality to the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and let ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ denote the corresponding constant for radial functions. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the operator norms ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ and ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ as the dimension $d$ tends to infinity. We further establish a dimension-free endpoint Stein-Tomas inequality for radial functions, together with the corresponding estimate for general functions which we prove with an $O(d^{1/2})$ dependence. Our methods rely on a uniform two-sided refinement of Stempak's asymptotic $L^p$ estimate of Bessel functions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 57 (8) 2025
item.dc:creator: Diogo Oliveira e Silva, B{\l}a\.zej Wr\'obel

item.title: Medians, Oscillations, and Distance Functions
item.description: arXiv:2507.21020v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vasin (for $n=1$) and Anderson, Lehrb\"ack, Mudarra, and V\"ah\"akangas (arXiv:2209.06284) (for $n>1$) provided a geometric characterization of the sets $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for which $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-\alpha}$ is a Muckenhoupt $A_1$ weight for some $\alpha > 0$. In this paper, we provide a geometric characterization of the sets $E \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (which we call median porous sets) such that $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-\alpha}$ is a Muckenhoupt $A_p$ weight for some $\alpha > 0$ (given any $1 < p \leq \infty$). Given $1 < p \leq \infty$, we also find the precise range of exponents $\alpha$ for which $w = \operatorname{dist}(\cdot, E)^{-\alpha} \in A_p$, in analogy to the $p=1$ case done in arXiv:2209.06284. With our characterization, we prove that $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus E$ supports a Hardy-Sobolev inequality if $E$ is an appropriate median porous set. The proofs rely on a new median-value characterization of $BMO$: For a real-valued measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and constants $0 < s < t < 1$, \[\|f\|_{BMO} \approx_{s, t, n} \sup_{Q}[M_t(f, Q) - M_s(f, Q)]\] where $M_s(f, Q)$ denotes the $s$-median value of $f$ on $Q$.
item.dc:creator: Marcus Pasquariello, Ignacio Uriarte-Tuero

item.title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter
item.description: arXiv:2603.25998v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the concentration of the Fourier transform changes the integrability threshold imposed by the size of its spectral support. Let $\mu$ be a positive Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $0\ne f\in L^2(\mu)$ with $f\mu$ compactly supported. Suppose that $\operatorname{supp}(f\mu)$ can be covered by $O(r^{-\alpha})$ balls of radius $r$, where $0<\alpha<n$. If the normalized Fourier ratio of $f\mu$ has decay exponent $\kappa<\frac{\alpha}{2}$, then $\widehat{f\mu}\notin L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for $$2\leq p<\frac{2(n-2\kappa)}{\alpha-2\kappa},$$ and at $\kappa=\frac{\alpha}{2}$ every finite $p$ is excluded. A uniform power bound for the Fourier ratio excludes the finite critical endpoint as well. We prove that the strict range is sharp for every admissible pair $(\alpha,\kappa)$ by convolving a Salem measure with a Cantor measure whose digits are consecutive and whose bases increase, and the resulting support has Hausdorff dimension exactly $\alpha$. We also obtain necessary conditions for Fourier extension estimates and compute the Fourier ratio exponent for smooth densities on hypersurfaces whose second fundamental form has constant rank.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Deodhar, Alex Iosevich

item.title: Liouville regular Jordan curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.11598v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.
item.dc:creator: Tomohiro Asano, Yuichi Ike

item.title: Pointwise estimates for an anisotropic product type singular integral on the sphere
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Abdelhakim

item.title: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
item.description: arXiv:2411.16266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.
item.dc:creator: Dario Giandinoto

item.title: Linear Response for Bernoulli Convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2604.20883v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mu_{\lambda}$ be the Bernoulli convolution measure with parameter $\lambda\in(0,1)$. We study the regularity of the function %We prove that $h=h_{\phi}:\lambda\mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(x)\,d\mu_{\lambda}(x)$ for H\"older observables $\phi$. We describe sufficient conditions for both smoothness and non smoothness of this function. In particular, we show that for almost every function with respect to certain Wiener like measures on $C[0,1]$, $h_\phi$ exhibits a phase transition: it is almost nowhere differentiable for small $\lambda$ and it is almost everywhere differentiable for large $\lambda.$
item.dc:creator: Jianning Fu

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-i\omega I)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.02155v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mawhin, Jorge Novoa
